features.summary: Four public screens (/login, /login/2fa, /login/setup-2fa, /set-password) run a two-step staff sign-in through Refine's authProvider (src/app/providers/authProvider.ts). GET /admin/auth/me then feeds identity, every permission gate and 'your address' (lastLoginIp). Logout ends the server session; invite/reset links and the forced change of a temporary password both go through POST /admin/auth/password/set.

endpoints.request: `{email,password}` JSON. Email is trimmed by the client (SignInForm.tsx:65); match it case-insensitively (mock session.ts:199-201). Public: no session and no CSRF check (ignore a stale X-CSRF-Token the client may still send). Server order: IP rules first (map scenario admin-team step 5, ip-rules step 3) → rate limit per email+IP (backend decision 021) → credentials → suspended → create the pre-2FA session. Revoke/replace any session cookie already on the request (fixation).
endpoints.response: `{next}`: `password` when must_change_password (checked first), else `totp` when twofa_enabled, else `totp_setup` (mock session.ts:216). The client routes to /set-password, /login/2fa or /login/setup-2fa (authProvider.ts:24-28) and treats a missing/unknown value as `totp` (authProvider.ts:70). Sets the pre-2FA session cookie (httpOnly) and the readable CSRF cookie (VITE_CSRF_COOKIE, default `csrf_token`) and repeats the token in the `X-CSRF-Token` response header (session.ts:213-217). last_login_* are NOT written yet (they are set at the 2FA step).

businessRules: 2FA is mandatory: no full session without a TOTP code (staff_users description; admin surface "staff session + 2FA + permission").

IP rules run before the password on login and before authentication on every /admin route: active block (scope admin|all) or restriction on + IP not allowlisted → 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED, and the deciding rule gets hit_count+1 / last_hit_at (map ip-rules step 3; backend decision 028).
A suspended account is refused with 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED even with the right password, and none of its old sessions work (map admin-team step 8).

Pre-2FA session scope: only POST /admin/auth/2fa, /2fa/setup (2FA off), /password/set without token (must_change_password) and /logout accept it; every other route answers 401 (mock requireSession stages, session.ts:103-121). Short lifetime (proposed 10 min).
next order at login: must_change_password → password; else twofa_enabled → totp; else totp_setup (session.ts:216).

Without a token, POST /admin/auth/password/set is allowed only for a pre-2FA session whose staff member has must_change_password=true; otherwise a stolen password alone could change the password without the TOTP step (the mock only checks the pre-2FA stage, session.ts:287-291).
last_login_at and last_login_ip are written at 2FA completion from the request (map admin-team step 5); the console uses lastLoginIp as the caller's address.
status 'invited' becomes 'active' at the first full sign-in (staff_users description).
Invite/reset tokens are stored as hashes, valid 1 h, single use (auth_tokens description); setting a password consumes the token and ends all sessions of the account.

A temporary password forces a change before anything else (next=password); passwords and TOTP secrets never appear in later responses, logs or audit entries (POST /admin/staff/:id/password description).
Rate limits with Retry-After on login, 2fa, 2fa/setup and password/set (backend decision 021).
CSRF: every mutation that carries a session needs a matching X-CSRF-Token (decision 006); login and token-mode password/set have no session to bind to (rely on SameSite cookies + Origin check).

questions.question: Session lifetime and idle timeout for staff sessions?
questions.proposedAnswer: Absolute 8 h (the mock seeds staff expiresAt ≤ now+8 h, src/mocks/sessions.ts:59), sliding idle timeout 30 min via last_seen_at (writes throttled to ~1/min), pre-2FA stage 10 min. Expiry shows up as 401 on the next call; the console has no idle timer.

questions.question: Rotate the session token and the CSRF token when 2FA completes?
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes: new session token at the 2FA step (fixation defence); if the CSRF token changes, set the cookie and the X-CSRF-Token header in the same 204 (the client re-reads it, csrf.ts:30-33).

questions.question: Order of checks at login?
questions.proposedAnswer: IP rules → rate limit → credentials (401) → suspended (403) → pre-2FA session + next. Suspension is revealed only to someone with the right password.
questions.basis: map admin-team steps 5 and 8; mock session.ts:199-216; decisions 021/028

questions.question: TOTP parameters and issuer name?
questions.proposedAnswer: RFC 6238: SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 s step, ±1 step drift; issuer from config (mock uses "GSM Supply") and the staff email as the account label.

questions.question: What happens to outstanding invite/reset tokens?
questions.proposedAnswer: A new link voids older unused links of the account; setting the password voids all; suspension voids all (later use → 410 TOKEN_INVALID).

questions.question: Should 2fa/setup be refused once 2FA is enabled?
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes, 409 TWOFA_ALREADY_ENABLED; re-enrolment only after an Owner runs POST /admin/staff/:id/reset-2fa.
questions.basis: map admin-team step 9 (reset-2fa is the recovery path)

questions.question: Could GET /admin/auth/me carry the maintenance state so every staff member sees the banner (MISMATCHES M201, system-health question 4)?
questions.proposedAnswer: Not needed now: the banner reads GET /admin/system/health for system:read staff. If wanted later, add an optional me.maintenance object; the console ignores unknown fields until then.
questions.basis: M201; map system-integrity scenario (admin keeps working during checkout maintenance)

questions.question: Self-service password change or 2FA re-enrolment for a signed-in staff member?
questions.proposedAnswer: None: the map has no such routes; recovery is an Owner sending a reset link (POST /admin/staff/:id/password) or resetting 2FA. The sign-in form only says "Ask an Owner to send you a reset link".

questions.question: Does POST /admin/auth/password/set sign the person in?
questions.proposedAnswer: No. Answer 204 and revoke sessions; the console always sends the person to /login?reason=password-set and a normal sign-in follows (next = totp or totp_setup).

questions.question: A signed-in staff member gets must_change_password=true (temporary password set with revokeSessions=false): what happens to the open session?
questions.proposedAnswer: The session keeps working: the console never redirects on me.mustChangePassword, so blocking routes would only produce errors. The change is forced at the next sign-in (next=password). The dialog defaults to revokeSessions=true, so this is rare.

JSON is camelCase in both directions (types.ts:2); request bodies are JSON with Content-Type application/json (client.ts:62-69).
Every request uses credentials:"include" and Accept: application/json (downloads */*) (client.ts:58-60, 78-84, 165).
Non-GET requests carry X-CSRF-Token when the client has one (client.ts:71-74; csrf.ts:25-33); GETs must never change state (queries are retried once on 5xx/network, useApiQuery.ts:26-28).

Errors are application/problem+json {type,title,status,code,detail,errors[]} (errors.ts:185-208); title and detail are shown verbatim to staff, so write user-facing English; always send code (else the client invents HTTP_<status>, errors.ts:64).

errors[] items: {field, message} (field may also be path/pointer/name/param; message may be detail/title/code); dotted paths like items.0.name, JSON pointers accepted, a leading body. is stripped (errors.ts:100-164). Field names must equal the request body keys (camelCase).
X-Request-Id on every response (errors.ts:205; ErrorState.tsx:31-35 shows it); body.requestId accepted as a fallback.
429 must carry Retry-After in seconds or as an HTTP date (errors.ts:166-173); the UI shows the wait.

Session-ending codes: any 401, and 403 with code ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED or IP_NOT_ALLOWED, sign the CALLER out wherever they appear (authProvider.ts:43-54, 97-105; useApiMutation.ts:66). Never use them for business refusals about another record (a suspended customer or staff target, an IP-rule validation error, a wrong secret in an authenticated action).
403 FORBIDDEN never signs out (authProvider.ts:97-98); its detail should name the missing permission like the UI hint "You need the x:y permission" (accessControlProvider.ts:40-41).
204 or an empty body means no result (client.ts:96-99); a 2xx with a non-JSON body throws INVALID_RESPONSE (client.ts:100-111), so never answer text or HTML on success.
Creates may answer 201 or 200 (any 2xx is accepted; the mocks use 201); deletes answer 204 and the data provider hands Refine the id (dataProvider.ts:98-106).
Lists: JSON array + x-total-count = total matching rows before the range (client.ts:140-153); without the header, pagers, tab counts and "Show more" break. Count-only calls use _start=0&_end=1.

CORS: exact console origin + Allow-Credentials on every /admin and /health response including errors; expose x-total-count, x-request-id, x-csrf-token, retry-after, content-disposition (decision 006 `5); a CORS refusal surfaces as NETWORK_ERROR with status 0 (errors.ts:80-89).
Base URL: VITE_API_BASE_URL (config.ts:3-7); /admin/* and /health live under the same base; the dev proxy forwards /admin and /health (vite.config.ts).
A 404 on a show endpoint renders a not-found view (MerchantDetail.tsx:62, useCustomer.ts:20, TicketThread.tsx:49, IncidentDrawer.tsx:28): always answer problem+json NOT_FOUND.
Permissions: CRUD rows x:* mean x:read/create/update/delete per operation (M7, permissions.ts:32-41); granted x:* covers every x:action; a required x:* needs x:* or * (permissions.ts:11-18).
The client caches GET /admin/auth/me for 60 s (meCache.ts:15): enforce permission and role changes on the next request server-side; never snapshot permissions per session.
Query strings come from URLSearchParams: space as +, repeated keys for arrays, booleans "true"/"false", empty values omitted (query.ts:11-22); accept string or string[] for every filter.
All server strings are rendered as text, never HTML; the UI limits labels to 60 chars, block reasons to 120 and notes to 140, but the server must validate lengths itself.

Proposed new error codes (not referenced by the frontend; the UI shows any code's title/detail): TWOFA_ALREADY_ENABLED, CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_ROLE, SELF_LOCKOUT, TWOFA_NOT_ENABLED; reuse NOT_SUSPENDED and LAST_OWNER for staff.

Test-only placeholder codes in frontend tests (X, BOOM, REFUSED, A1, B2, FIVE, FIRST_CODE, SECOND_CODE, THIRD_CODE, WITH_ISSUE, WITHOUT_ISSUE) are not server codes; country/currency literals (GB, USD, SEK…) only matched the scan.

The mock layer checks no permissions (except system-health and supplier writes) and fakes only simple state changes (decision 014; src/test/mockApi.ts:36-40); rules missing from the mocks still apply (see each endpoint's mapConflict).

Lockout guards (restriction on, self-block, last allow rule) must use the real request IP from a trusted proxy chain; the console's own hints use me.lastLoginIp (M15), so keep last_login_ip = the IP of the current sign-in.

# Staff sign-in flow (as the console implements it)

Screens: `/login` (LoginPage), `/login/2fa` (TwoFactorPage), `/login/setup-2fa` (SetupTwoFactorPage), `/set-password[?token=]` (SetPasswordPage), all public (src/features/auth/paths.ts). Refine's authProvider (src/app/providers/authProvider.ts) drives them. A safe in-console `?to=<path>` travels through every step (destination.ts) and is where a finished sign-in lands; without it `/` forwards to the first page the role may open (HomeRedirect.tsx).

## 1. POST /admin/auth/login `{email, password}`
- Client trims the email. No session exists yet, so no CSRF check (the client may still send a stale X-CSRF-Token: ignore it).
- Server order: IP rules (403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) → rate limit (429 + Retry-After) → credentials (401 UNAUTHORIZED, identical for unknown email, wrong password, or no password chosen yet) → suspended (403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED) → create the pre-2FA session.
- 200 `{next}`: `password` (must_change_password, checked first) | `totp` (twofa_enabled) | `totp_setup` (first enrolment). Client routes: password → /set-password (no token), totp → /login/2fa, totp_setup → /login/setup-2fa (authProvider.ts:24-28); unknown → /login/2fa.
- Cookies on the 200: session cookie (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/; short pre-2FA lifetime, proposed 10 min) + readable CSRF cookie named by VITE_CSRF_COOKIE (default `csrf_token`, not httpOnly, readable by the console origin) + the same token in the `X-CSRF-Token` response header (mock session.ts:213-217).
- UI per error: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with `errors[{field:'email'|'password'}]` → under the fields; 401 → fixed "Email or password is incorrect" + request id, password cleared (authErrors.ts:35-43); 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED → "This account is suspended" card; 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED → "Sign-in is not allowed from this network" card (SignInBlocked.tsx); 429 → "Too many sign-in attempts … Try again in N seconds/minutes" from Retry-After; anything else → banner with the server title/detail + request id.

## 2a. POST /admin/auth/2fa `{code}` (from /login/2fa)
- Needs the pre-2FA cookie + X-CSRF-Token. Exactly 6 digits (client strips other characters).
- 204 → the session becomes full: rotate the session token (and the CSRF token if desired: then set the cookie and send X-CSRF-Token in this response); set last_login_at/last_login_ip from this request; invited → active on the first full sign-in; audit. The client invalidates its auth cache, calls GET /admin/auth/me, then opens `?to=` or `/`.
- 422 VALIDATION_FAILED `errors[{field:'code'}]` → under the field, code selected; 401 (pre-2FA session expired) → banner + "Back to sign in"; 403 CSRF_FAILED → banner; 429 → banner with the wait.

## 2b. First enrolment (next = totp_setup, /login/setup-2fa)
- POST /admin/auth/2fa/setup (no body, CSRF) once per visit → 200 `{secret, otpauthUrl, qrSvg?}` (qrSvg = raw SVG markup); "Retry" asks again and the new pending secret replaces the old one (useTwoFactorSetup.ts).
- Then POST /admin/auth/2fa `{code}` with the first code → as 2a; the server confirms the pending secret and sets twofa_enabled=true.
- Setup errors: 401 → signed out to /login; anything else → "Could not start the setup" + server detail + Retry. Refuse setup when 2FA is already enabled (proposed 409 TWOFA_ALREADY_ENABLED).

## 2c. Forced password change (next = password)
- /set-password without a token: POST /admin/auth/password/set `{password}` with the pre-2FA cookie + CSRF → 204 → server clears must_change_password and ends the pre-2FA session (mock resetSession) → client opens `/login?reason=password-set` ("Password updated. Sign in with your new password.") → the person signs in again → next = totp or totp_setup.

## 3. GET /admin/auth/me
- After 2FA and on every navigation (client cache 60 s, meCache.ts). 200 Me: id, email, name, status, role {id,name}, permissions (drive every gate), twofaEnabled, mustChangePassword, lastLoginAt, lastLoginIp (the console's "your address"). Send X-CSRF-Token on this response too: it is the first call after every reload, and a cross-site console cannot read the CSRF cookie.

## Invite and reset links
- Emailed link: `<console>/set-password?token=<token>` (auth_tokens: hash only, 1 h, single use). POST /admin/auth/password/set `{token, password}` → 204 (no session is created) → `/login?reason=password-set` → normal sign-in (a new staff member then gets next = totp_setup).
- 410 TOKEN_INVALID → the form is replaced by a dead-link card with the server detail ("Ask an Owner to send you a new link." is added only when the server gave no detail); 422 WEAK_PASSWORD or any `errors[{field:'password'}]` → under "New password"; anything else → banner. The console hints at least 10 characters.
- There is no self-service "forgot password" route: the form only says "Ask an Owner to send you a reset link."

## Logout
- POST /admin/auth/logout (CSRF) → 204, revoke the session, clear both cookies (Max-Age=0). 401 means already signed out and counts as success; any other failure keeps the user signed in with an error toast. The client then forgets its in-memory CSRF token and me cache and lands on /login without ?to=.

## Session expiry and idle handling
- No client idle timer: the server owns absolute and idle expiry (proposed 8 h absolute, 30 min idle, 10 min pre-2FA). Any 401 on any request → the client clears the me cache, runs logout (a 401 there is fine) and redirects to `/login?to=<current path>`, where the form says "Sign in to continue to <path>". Role or permission changes reach the UI within the 60 s me cache; the server must apply them on the next request.

## 401 versus 403 (authProvider.ts:43-54, 97-105)
- 401 UNAUTHORIZED: no, expired, revoked or pre-2FA session → sign out. Exceptions: on the login form it means "wrong email or password"; on the 2FA and set-password forms it shows as a banner.
- 403 FORBIDDEN: signed in but missing the permission → never signs out; shown in place (detail should name the permission).
- 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED: the caller's account is suspended → sign out to `/login?reason=suspended`.
- 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED: the caller's IP is refused (block or console restriction) → sign out to `/login?reason=ip`. Decided per request, before authentication.
- These three codes end the caller's session wherever they appear: never reuse them for refusals about other records (a suspended target account, an IP-rule validation error).
- 403 CSRF_FAILED: stays signed in, shows the error. 5xx, 429 and network failures never sign out (429 shows the wait from Retry-After).

## CSRF
- The client sends X-CSRF-Token on every non-GET request when it has a token: the readable cookie (VITE_CSRF_COOKIE, default csrf_token) first, else the last X-CSRF-Token response header kept in memory (lost on reload) (csrf.ts:25-33).
- Server: validate on every mutation that carries a session (2fa, 2fa/setup, password/set without token, logout and all /admin mutations); there is nothing to validate on login and token-mode password/set. Send X-CSRF-Token on the login, 2fa and me responses.

# Permissions

## Grammar and matching
- `<area>:<action>`, lower snake_case on both sides (`staff:read`, `wallet:credit_limit`, `api_keys:revoke`). `<area>:*` = every action of the area; `*` = everything; the client also accepts `*:*` as `*` (src/lib/auth/permissions.ts:5-9).
- Granted g covers required r when g = r, g = `*`/`*:*`, or g = `x:*` and r starts with `x:`. A list of required permissions means any-of (permissions.ts:15-18). The server must match the same way.
- A REQUIRED `x:*` is covered only by `x:*` or `*`, never by the set of concrete `x:…` actions (permissions.ts:11-14). Only two action rows need a literal wildcard: `PUT /admin/risk/rules` → `risk:*` and `POST /admin/content-pages/generate` → `storefront:*`.

## CRUD mapping (MISMATCHES M7)
- Manifest CRUD rows carry `x:*`; the operation decides the concrete permission: list/show → `x:read`, create (POST) → `x:create`, update (PATCH) → `x:update`, delete → `x:delete` (crudPermission, permissions.ts:32-41; accessControlProvider.ts:14-26). Action rows carry their exact permission. `/admin/auth/*` need none (public or session only); `GET /health` is public.
- Access feature: staff:read (GET /admin/staff, /:id), staff:create (POST /admin/staff), staff:update (PATCH, /password, /sessions/revoke, /reset-2fa), staff:suspend (/suspend, /reactivate); access:read (GET /admin/ip-rules, /:id, POST /check), access:create (POST /admin/ip-rules), access:delete (DELETE), access:update (PUT /admin/access/restriction); roles:read (GET /admin/roles, /:id, GET /admin/permissions), roles:create/update/delete; sessions:read, sessions:revoke; audit:read (GET /admin/audit-logs, /:id). Reading the restriction state needs settings:read (GET /admin/settings).

## Where the console checks (always from GET /admin/auth/me .permissions, cached 60 s)
- Page gate: each page resource's meta.permission (src/app/resources.ts; any-of lists from the feature manifests). access: staff:read | access:read | roles:read | sessions:read; finance: ledger:read | payments:read | invoices:read | reports:read | reports:finance; merchants: clients:read | groups:read | kyc:read; refunds: refunds:read | disputes:read | reports:finance; services: catalog:read | pricing:read | inventory:read; storefront: storefront:read | legal:read | catalog:read; settings: settings:read | payments:gateways | tax:read | notifications:read | webhooks:read; system-health: system:read | alerts:read | incidents:read; single permission: dashboard:read, orders:read, customers:read, support:read, risk:read, growth:read (checkouts), suppliers:read, commissions:read, audit:read. Without it the ForbiddenPage shows; `/` forwards to the first permitted page.
- Tabs: shown only with their read permission (e.g. AccessPage.tsx TABS).
- Buttons and links: `needs('x:y')` disables the control with the title "You need the x:y permission" (useAccessGrants.ts:20-24); deep links show only when useCanOpenPage allows the target page (M44).
- `can({ action })`: an action containing a colon is the permission itself; a CRUD action maps through the resource meta; the refusal reason reads "You need the <perm> permission" (accessControlProvider.ts:19-42).
- All of this is a hint: every route enforces its permission; 403 FORBIDDEN (detail naming the missing permission) never signs out.

## GET /admin/permissions (roles:read)
- The whole catalog, no paging: `string[]` (mock: the 115 concrete keys of the manifest, src/mocks/roles.ts:44-89) or `[{key, label?, group?}]`; normalised client-side (access/lib/permissions.ts:30-45: label defaults to the humanised action, group to the prefix; order kept, duplicates dropped). No wildcards in the catalog; wildcard or unknown entries already on a role are shown under "Other entries" (permissions.ts:57-76).
- The role summary groups prefixes into nine areas: Orders (orders, inventory, files), Customers (customers, clients, wallet, groups, kyc, api_keys, growth), Support (support), Risk (risk), Money (ledger, payments, invoices, commissions, refunds, disputes, reports), Catalog (catalog, pricing, suppliers, storefront, legal), Settings (settings, tax, currencies, webhooks, notifications), Admins (staff, access, roles, sessions, audit, queues), System (system, alerts, incidents); dashboard belongs to none (permissions.ts:85-119). Levels (full / view / partial / none) are computed against the catalog, so the catalog must list every permission the server checks.

## Roles
- `{id, name, permissions: string[], staffCount?}`; permissions stored as given (`*`, `x:*`, concrete keys); me.permissions = the role's list. Roles are editable records (M11); a role held by anyone cannot be deleted (409 ROLE_IN_USE).
- Owner: the console treats a member of a role named "Owner" or of any role containing `*` as an Owner (staffGuards.ts:16-19, M18); the mock server uses the name "Owner" (accessStaff.ts:202-208). Proposed server rule: role contains `*`.

## Built-in roles (mock seed only, src/mocks/roles.ts; MISMATCHES M11, M198)
- 1 Owner: `["*"]`.
- 2 Admin: dashboard:read; `x:*` for orders, inventory, files, customers, clients, wallet, groups, kyc, api_keys, growth, support, risk, ledger, payments, invoices, commissions, refunds, disputes, reports, catalog, pricing, suppliers, storefront, legal, settings, tax, currencies, webhooks, notifications, system, alerts, incidents; read only for staff, access, roles, sessions, audit, queues.
- 3 Finance: dashboard:read; `x:read` for orders, inventory, files, customers, clients, wallet, groups, kyc, api_keys, growth, risk, catalog, pricing, suppliers, storefront, legal, system, alerts, incidents; `x:*` for ledger, payments, invoices, commissions, refunds, disputes, reports.
- 4 Support: dashboard:read; `x:read` for orders, inventory, files, risk, catalog, pricing, suppliers, storefront, legal, system, alerts, incidents; `x:*` for customers, clients, wallet, groups, kyc, api_keys, growth, support.
- 5 Risk reviewer: dashboard:read; `x:read` for orders, inventory, files, customers, clients, wallet, groups, kyc, api_keys, growth, support, ledger, payments, invoices, commissions, refunds, disputes, reports, system, alerts, incidents; `risk:*`.
- 6 Read only: dashboard:read; `x:read` for orders, inventory, files, customers, clients, wallet, groups, kyc, api_keys, growth, support, risk, ledger, payments, invoices, commissions, refunds, disputes, reports, catalog, pricing, suppliers, storefront, legal, system, alerts, incidents (no settings, no admin areas).
- The `?mock=readonly` scenario signs everyone in with the Read only role (session.ts:143-148).

# List conventions (simple-rest dialect)

## What the console sends (src/lib/api/query.ts, src/app/providers/dataProvider.ts)
- Range: `_start` (0-based, inclusive) and `_end` (exclusive). Page N of size S → `_start=(N-1)*S&_end=N*S` (query.ts:97-114). Every list call sends a range (Refine pagination mode 'server'). Sizes in use: 25 (paged tables, sessions, audit "Show more"), 200 (whole short lists: staff, roles, and the merchants/commissions/storefront caps), 500 (IP rules per kind), 1 (count-only calls `_start=0&_end=1` that read only x-total-count: tab counts and figure strips in orders, merchants, customers, finance (payments), refunds, risk, services, storefront, commissions, support).
- Sort: `_sort=f1,f2&_order=asc,desc`, comma lists in the same order (query.ts:41-42), camelCase field names, only the fields each screen offers (e.g. support tickets `_sort=late,updatedAt`).
- Search: `q=<text>` (query.ts:43; a Refine filter on the pseudo field `q`, query.ts:75-86). Meaning: case-insensitive substring over endpoint-specific fields (mock searchFields; default every top-level string field, crud.ts:93-106). Access/audit: staff → name, email; roles → name; ip-rules → cidr, label, reason; sessions → ip, subject.name, subject.email; audit → actorName, action, entityLabel.
- Field filters: `field=value` = equality on the camelCase response field; a repeated key = IN (`status=a&status=b`, `id=1&id=2`); operator suffixes `_ne` (repeated = NOT IN), `_gte`, `_lte`, `_gt`, `_lt`, `_like` (case-insensitive contains) (query.ts:47-55; crud.ts:24-35). Refine 'or'/'and' and any other operator are rejected client-side (query.ts:76-93).
- Values: strings as typed; numbers as decimal text; booleans `true`/`false`; Date objects become ISO UTC strings (query.ts:57-61); undefined, null and '' are never sent (query.ts:17); URLSearchParams encoding (space = '+', parse it as a space).
- getMany (Refine): one list call `id=<a>&id=<b>&_start=0&_end=<n>` (dataProvider.ts:63-74).

## What the console expects back
- 200 JSON array of rows + `x-total-count: <rows matching the filters, before the range>` (client.ts:140-153). A missing or non-numeric header makes total = rows received, which breaks pagers, tab counts, "Show more" and "not all shown" notes. Expose the header through CORS.
- How the mock list engine answers (crud.ts:112-137, applyListQuery): filters (text equality; numeric or ISO-string comparison for range operators; dotted paths such as `role.id`) → `q` → multi-field sort (numbers numerically, otherwise localeCompare with numeric collation; nulls last ascending, first descending) → `slice(_start, _end)`. No `_sort` → insertion order (≈ id asc). No `_end` → to the end. x-total-count + `access-control-expose-headers`.
- Server proposal: whitelist sort and filter fields per endpoint (unknown → 422 VALIDATION_FAILED naming `_sort` or the field), a stable documented default order when `_sort` is absent (staff: createdAt asc; roles: id asc; sessions: lastSeenAt desc; ip-rules and audit: createdAt desc, which the console sends anyway), exact counts, and a maximum page of at least 500 (IP rules ask for 500).

## Endpoints that deviate
- Plain arrays with no paging and no x-total-count: GET /admin/permissions, GET /admin/orders/:id/events, GET /admin/clients/:id/api-keys, GET /admin/reports/suppliers, GET /admin/reports/top-clients; replace-all PUTs that answer arrays: PUT /admin/services/:id/fields, /group-prices, /options, /supplier-links.
- Objects, not arrays: GET /admin/settings (one flat key → value object), GET /admin/auth/me, GET /health and every summary/report GET (system-health, dashboard, reports).
- Extra list parameters: GET /admin/audit-logs `from`/`to` (YYYY-MM-DD, both days included; UTC in the mock) with `actorType`/`actorId`/`entityType`; GET /admin/commission-accruals `createdAt_gte`; GET /admin/incidents `open=true`; GET /admin/support-tickets multi-field `_sort=late,updatedAt`; repeated keys on GET /admin/content-pages `kind`, GET /admin/customers `riskLevel`, GET /admin/data-requests `status`, GET /admin/support-tickets `status`; path-scoped lists GET /admin/clients/:id/statement, GET /admin/suppliers/:id/services, GET /admin/system/queues/:name/failed (`_sort=failedAt&_order=desc`).
- Loaded whole and sorted/filtered/counted client-side (cap → "not all shown" note when total is larger): /admin/staff (200, no sort sent), /admin/roles (200), /admin/ip-rules (500 per kind, `kind` filter, createdAt desc), plus short lookups in other features (groups, suppliers, reply templates).
- No endpoint uses cursor paging (audit question 7 asks; the console dedupes by id instead).

# Headers, cookies and CORS

## Request headers the console sends (src/lib/api/client.ts)
- `Accept: application/json` on every call (client.ts:58-60); `Accept: */*` for downloads (apiDownload, client.ts:159-170: orders export, customer data export, merchant statement PDF).
- `Content-Type: application/json` whenever a body is sent (client.ts:62-69). No multipart uploads exist in the console.
- `X-CSRF-Token: <token>` on every non-GET request when the client knows a token (client.ts:71-74; csrf.ts:25-33).
- `Idempotency-Key`: possible through ApiInit.headers (client.ts:10-11), but no admin call sends it (the manifest requires it only on POST /store/v1/checkout-sessions/:token/pay).
- Cookies via `credentials: 'include'` on every fetch, GET /health included (client.ts:78-84). No Authorization header, no X-Requested-With; the browser adds Origin.

## Response headers the console reads
- `x-total-count` (lists, client.ts:149), `X-Request-Id` (every error and INVALID_RESPONSE, errors.ts:205, client.ts:108; shown as "Request <id>"; body.requestId/request_id accepted as fallback), `Retry-After` (429; seconds or an HTTP date, errors.ts:166-173), `X-CSRF-Token` (any response; remembered in memory, csrf.ts:29-33), `Content-Disposition` (downloads; `filename*=UTF-8''…` wins over `filename="…"`, download.ts:3-17), `Content-Type` (JSON or problem+json; any JSON error body is parsed).

## Cookies
- Session: httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/; a name distinct from the merchant portal's session cookie (both live on the API host); short pre-2FA lifetime, then the full-session lifetime; never readable by JS. Cleared (Max-Age=0) on logout.
- CSRF: readable (not httpOnly) cookie named `csrf_token` (VITE_CSRF_COOKIE), Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, with a Domain the console origin can read (e.g. `Domain=.example.com` for console admin.example.com + API api.example.com); value bound to the session (synchronizer token or HMAC double-submit). Issued at login, rotated with the session at 2FA if desired, cleared at logout. The mock writes `csrf_token=<token>; path=/; SameSite=Lax` (session.ts:64-68).
- Cross-site deployment (console and API on different registrable domains): the session cookie must be SameSite=None; Secure, and the console cannot read the CSRF cookie, so it lives on the X-CSRF-Token response header: send it on login, 2fa and me (me is the first call after every reload).
- Plain links (`/admin/files/:id` downloads, the Bull Board link `/admin/queues`) are top-level navigations that rely on the session cookie; SameSite=Lax sends it on top-level GET.

## CORS (when VITE_API_BASE_URL is another origin)
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <exact console origin from config>` (never `*`), `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, `Vary: Origin` on EVERY /admin/* and /health response, errors included: without them the browser hides the answer and the client sees NETWORK_ERROR (status 0), so a 401 would not even sign out.
- Preflight (OPTIONS): `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE`; `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, X-CSRF-Token, Idempotency-Key, Accept`; `Access-Control-Max-Age: 600`. Answer preflights before IP rules, rate limits, auth and CSRF, so that the real request can carry a readable 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED.
- `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: x-total-count, x-request-id, x-csrf-token, retry-after, content-disposition` (decision 006 lists the first three; Retry-After and Content-Disposition are not CORS-safelisted, so expose them too).
- Same-origin deployment (reverse proxy, or the dev proxy VITE_DEV_PROXY_TARGET forwarding /admin and /health, vite.config.ts): no CORS, first-party cookies; VITE_API_BASE_URL is then empty.

## Other
- X-Request-Id on every response, success included; problem bodies may repeat it as requestId.
- Cache-Control: no-store on /admin/auth/* and on any answer carrying a secret (temporaryPassword, the 2FA secret).
- Problem responses: `Content-Type: application/problem+json` with `{type, title, status, code, detail, errors[]}`; 2xx bodies must be JSON or empty (client.ts:96-111).

# Mock layer (dev and tests only; decision 014)

## How it is built
- MSW 2 (`msw ^2.15`). Browser: src/mocks/browser.ts (`setupWorker`, started from main.tsx only when `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_API_MOCKS === 'true'`; the worker script src/mocks/worker/mockServiceWorker.js is served by a dev-only Vite plugin). Node/Vitest: src/mocks/node.ts exports `mockServer = setupServer(...handlers)`.
- Handler list (src/mocks/handlers/index.ts): `handlers` = sessionHandlers (src/mocks/session.ts: /admin/auth/*) + systemHandlers (GET /health) + accessHandlers (handlers/accessStaff.ts, accessIpRules.ts, accessRoles.ts, accessSessions.ts) + orders + ledger + settings (GET/PATCH /admin/settings) + every `src/features/*/mocks/index.ts` (each exports `mocks: FeatureMocks = { handlers, reset }`), found with `import.meta.glob(..., { eager: true })`. Specific routes come before `/:id`. `resetMockState()` resets the scenario, the session and every store.
- URL matching: handlers use `*/admin/...` (any origin); /health answers only at `<path of VITE_API_BASE_URL>/health` (handlers/system.ts:9-25).
- Seed: src/mocks/seed/demo-state.json (1.9 MB, `{capturedAt, state}` written by scripts/extract-demo-seed.mjs, which runs the demo's own data generator). Loaded with `import('./demo-state.json?raw')`; every timestamp is rebased to now (seed/index.ts:38-42); demo ids become numbers (`'ad1'` → 1, demoNumericId), money becomes 4-decimal strings (toMoney), times ISO strings (toIso). Stores are in-memory `Collection`s (db.ts: auto ids, PATCH merge) in src/mocks/staff.ts, roles.ts (6 demo roles + the permission catalog), ipRules.ts, sessions.ts, settings.ts, orders.ts, ledger.ts and each feature's mocks/store.ts.
- `problem(status, code, title, detail?, errors?)` (problem.ts) → application/problem+json with `type: urn:gsm:problem:<code>` and `X-Request-Id: mock-req-<n>`. Helpers notFound / invalid / conflict wrap it (handlers/accessShared.ts, features/*/mocks/http.ts).
- List engine: `applyListQuery` / `crudHandlers` (crud.ts) implement the simple-rest dialect and set `x-total-count` + `access-control-expose-headers`.
- Session: session.ts keeps ONE session `{staffId, stage: 'password' | 'signed-in', csrf}` in localStorage (an in-memory Map when storage is missing, e.g. under Node), not in cookies. `guard(request)` answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED without a signed-in session and 403 CSRF_FAILED when a mutation's X-CSRF-Token differs. Demo credentials: any seeded staff email + `demo-password`, TOTP `123456`, invite token `demo-token`. `startSignedInSession(id)` signs in without the calls (then read the token from the X-CSRF-Token header of GET /admin/auth/me).
- Scenarios: `?mock=healthy|degraded|outage|monitoring-down|partial-failure|maintenance|readonly` (scenario.ts, kept per tab in sessionStorage; switcher panel scenarioSwitcher.ts). `readonly` gives everyone the Read only role in me; `outage` makes /health down; system-health reads fail per scenario profile. In code: `setMockScenario(name)`.
- Limits: mocks fake responses and simple state changes; they do not re-implement server rules. No permission checks outside system-health and supplier writes, no IP rules on requests, no /16 / duplicate / lockout guards, no rate limits, invited staff can sign in with the demo password. Use them for shapes, status codes and the refusals they do implement.

## Harvesting one real example per route (recipe tested on 2026-10-31 with Vitest 4.1.12 and Node 26.4; it wrote nothing into the frontend repo)
1. Two files OUTSIDE the frontend repo, e.g. `backend/test/contract/harvest/vitest.config.mjs` and `harvest.test.ts`.
2. `vitest.config.mjs` is a plain object (a config outside the frontend cannot import `vitest/config`):
   `const FE = '/home/saifi/gsm-project/frontend-admin'; const HERE = '<absolute path of this folder>';`
   `export default { root: HERE, cacheDir: HERE + '/.cache', resolve: { alias: { '@': FE + '/src' } }, test: { globals: true, environment: 'node', execArgv: ['--no-experimental-webstorage'], include: ['harvest.test.ts'], env: { VITE_API_BASE_URL: 'http://api.test' }, server: { deps: { inline: ['@refinedev/react-router'] } }, css: false, testTimeout: 60000 } };`
   - root and cacheDir outside the frontend keep Vite/Vitest caches out of it. `@` is the only alias the mocks need. MODE is 'test', so latency() is skipped. VITE_API_BASE_URL without a path makes /health match `/health`. `globals: true` because a test file outside the frontend cannot resolve `vitest`. `--no-experimental-webstorage` is needed on Node ≥ 25 (its built-in localStorage). `environment: 'node'` works (the session falls back to the in-memory Map and the CSRF cookie write is skipped); use `'jsdom'` only to observe document.cookie.
3. `harvest.test.ts`: `import { mockServer } from '@/mocks/node'` (import msw only through this module, so one msw copy is used), `import { resetMockState } from '@/mocks/handlers'`, `import { DEMO_CODE, DEMO_PASSWORD, DEMO_INVITE_TOKEN } from '@/mocks/session'`, `import { setMockScenario } from '@/mocks/scenario'`. `beforeAll(() => mockServer.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }))`, `afterAll(() => mockServer.close())`. With plain `fetch` against `http://api.test`: POST /admin/auth/login `{email: 'rami@gsm-supply.example', password: DEMO_PASSWORD}` → read the X-CSRF-Token response header → POST /admin/auth/2fa `{code: DEMO_CODE}` with it → call each route, sending X-CSRF-Token on non-GET calls. Record `{status, headers (x-total-count, x-csrf-token, x-request-id, content-type, content-disposition), body}` per route and write the fixtures under the backend with absolute paths (writeFileSync).
4. Run with Node, not Bun (the mocks need Vite transforms: import.meta.glob, `?raw` imports, import.meta.env): `/home/saifi/gsm-project/frontend-admin/node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config <backend>/test/contract/harvest/vitest.config.mjs`.
5. Normalise before comparing: timestamps are rebased to the run time, CSRF tokens and temporary passwords are random, request ids count up. Compare shapes, types and status codes, not values. Call `resetMockState()` (and `setMockScenario`) between groups. Refusals are harvested by sending the input a handler checks (e.g. POST /admin/staff with rami@gsm-supply.example → 409 EMAIL_TAKEN; POST /admin/staff/1/suspend as Rami → 409 CANNOT_SUSPEND_SELF).
- Seed ids: staff 1 Rami (Owner, allowlisted 203.0.113.24), 2 Lina (Support), 3 Omar (Finance), 4 Dana (Admin), 5 Nadia (invited, no 2FA), 6 Yusuf (suspended); roles 1-6; IP rules 1-7 (3 allow, 4 block); audit entries 1-42; sessions 1-7 (4 staff, then 3 merchants). The restriction (adminAllowlistOnly) starts ON.
